method: Both pages fetched directly with curl and converted from HTML to text. Claims are verbatim-checked against the retrieved text of their own source with scripts/verify.py --only-source. Prose paraphrases; source_text stays verbatim. The national Otitis Media Guidelines clinical algorithms are delivered by app and PDF and were NOT retrieved; only the public burden and mechanism text was, and the gap is recorded in Unresolved. No antibiotic agent or dose is reconstructed.

claims.claim: Do not accept otitis media as the sole diagnosis in a sick febrile young child
claims.source_text: Do not accept otitis media as the sole diagnosis in a sick febrile young child without exclusion of more serious causes

claims.claim: Diagnosis requires acute onset plus inflammation and effusion
claims.source_text: Diagnosis requires acute onset and an abnormal ear examination with signs of middle ear inflammation and middle ear effusion

claims.claim: Avoid routine antibiotics for AOM
claims.source_text: Avoid the routine use of antibiotic treatment for acute otitis media

claims.claim: 75% have an episode by school age, peak 6-18 months
claims.source_text: 75% of children have at least one episode by school age … Peak age prevalence is 6-18 months

claims.claim: Household cigarette smoke is a modifiable risk factor
claims.source_text: Exposure to cigarette smoke from household contacts is a known modifiable risk factor

claims.claim: A red TM alone is not AOM
claims.source_text: a red TM alone is not AOM. The most common cause is a viral upper respiratory tract infection (URTI)

claims.claim: Normal tympanic membrane appearance
claims.source_text: TM is translucent … The handle of the malleus is vertical … No erythema

claims.claim: Injected tympanic membrane appearance
claims.source_text: Pink/red TM … Often seen with fever, eustachian tube obstruction or viral URTI … TM is transparent (there is no middle ear effusion) … The handle of the malleus is well seen and is more horizontal

claims.claim: AOM tympanic membrane appearance
claims.source_text: Loss of the TM landmarks, especially the handle of the malleus … TM is opaque, may be red from inflammation or white from pus in the middle ear

claims.claim: OME tympanic membrane appearance
claims.source_text: TM is retracted with prominence of the handle of the malleus, which is also drawn in/more horizontal … TM may be bulging or have an air-fluid level behind the TM … Yellow/amber appearance is consistent with fluid

claims.claim: Diagnosis is unreliable under 6 months
claims.source_text: the diagnosis of AOM and OME can be inaccurate. Other diagnoses should be fully considered

claims.claim: Most AOM resolves spontaneously without antibiotics
claims.source_text: Most cases of AOM in children resolve spontaneously and antibiotics are not recommended

claims.claim: Treat pain with regular simple analgesia
claims.source_text: Treat pain with adequate and regular simple analgesia

claims.claim: Topical analgesia adjunct on an intact tympanic membrane
claims.source_text: As an adjunct, short-term use of topical analgesia eg 2% lignocaine (for injection), 1-2 drops or Benzocaine + Phenazone (Auralgan ®) applied to an intact tympanic membrane, may be effective for severe acute ear pain

claims.claim: Decongestants, antihistamines and corticosteroids are not effective
claims.source_text: Decongestants, antihistamines and corticosteroids are not effective in AOM

claims.claim: No routine investigation; imaging only for suspected intracranial complications
claims.source_text: There is no role for routine diagnostic investigation for AOM … Diagnostic imaging such as CT and MRI is usually only required in children with suspected intracranial complications

claims.claim: Antimicrobial choice deferred to local susceptibility and guidelines
claims.source_text: Antimicrobial recommendations may vary according to local antimicrobial susceptibility patterns; please refer to local guidelines

claims.claim: Perforation is common and often relieves pain
claims.source_text: AOM with TM perforation is common and results in otorrhoea and frequently, relief of pain

claims.claim: Distinguish perforation otorrhoea from otitis externa
claims.source_text: Otorrhoea due to TM perforation should be distinguished from Otitis Externa

claims.claim: Otitis externa signs
claims.source_text: Ear is tender to examine … Skin of the external ear canal is swollen and there can be thin pus

claims.claim: Mastoiditis is the commonest suppurative complication
claims.source_text: Acute mastoiditis, although rare, is the most common suppurative complication of AOM and may be associated with intracranial complications

claims.claim: Mastoiditis diagnostic signs
claims.source_text: The diagnosis of AM is based on post auricular inflammatory signs (erythema, oedema, tenderness or fluctuance), a protruding auricle often with external auditory canal oedema and signs of AOM

claims.claim: Mastoiditis needs IV antibiotics and ENT
claims.source_text: Requires prompt treatment with appropriate … intravenous antibiotics (eg 3rd generation cephalosporin) … Consult ENT as may require surgical treatment

claims.claim: Facial nerve palsy and long-term complications
claims.source_text: Facial nerve palsy secondary to AOM should be discussed with ENT … Long-term non suppurative complications include atelectasis of the TM and cholesteatoma

claims.claim: OME definition
claims.source_text: OME, previously termed serous otitis or glue ear, is fluid in the middle ear without signs and symptoms of infection, other than transient hearing impairment

claims.claim: Effusion is not diagnostic of AOM and may persist 12 weeks
claims.source_text: The presence of a middle ear effusion is not a diagnostic sign of AOM (an effusion may not resolve for up to 12 weeks following AOM)

claims.claim: OME does not routinely need antibiotics or ENT referral
claims.source_text: Antibiotics and ENT referral are not routinely required for OME, as the majority of cases occur after an episode of AOM and resolve spontaneously with no long-term effects on language, literacy or cognitive development

claims.claim: Effusion beyond 3 months triggers hearing assessment and ENT
claims.source_text: Persistent effusion beyond 3 months should trigger a hearing assessment and ENT involvement/referral

claims.claim: Management differs for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children
claims.source_text: Management may also differ for children from higher … risk groups, such as those living in Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander … communities

claims.claim: Burden in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children
claims.source_text: Many Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander children, and almost all who live in remote communities, have middle ear infection, glue ear or runny ears (otitis media, OM). Children with OM cannot hear properly and have trouble with speech, language, learning and behaviour

claims.claim: All forms cause hearing loss with life-long impacts
claims.source_text: All forms of Otitis Media cause some level of hearing loss. If hearing loss persists it can cause social isolation with life-long impacts on communication, listening and understanding

claims.claim: School vulnerability and maltreatment risk
claims.source_text: Chronic otitis media and hearing loss increases a child's vulnerability on entering school, school attendance, and performance. … Children with hearing loss are more likely to experience child maltreatment

claims.claim: Pneumococcus and NTHi mechanism
claims.source_text: The germs called pneumococcus (pneumo) and non-typable H. influenzae (NTHi or H'flu) get into the baby or child's nose from other children. These germs can then get inside the middle ear and cause infection and pus - like a boil - which can burst the ear drum. Unlike a boil under the skin which can heal, the eardrum can take a long time to heal and must be treated. Germs in the nose also go inside the chest to cause pneumonia

claims.claim: OM may be asymptomatic and persist undetected
claims.source_text: Otitis Media may also be present without noticeable symptoms and can persist for long periods undetected
